name: Lookup Member Balance
description: look up member {member_id} in branch {branch_code} and read the savings balance

steps.description: Open lookup member balance at the entry URL.
Enter the member ID {member_id} into the Member ID field to begin the lookup.

target.robustness_note: Identifying the textbox 'Member ID'. 5 rung(s) verified against the live surface at record time. Rung 1 — role+name: the control exposes the accessible name 'Member ID', which survives restyling and DOM churn. Rung 1 — name alone: 'Member ID' identifies it without relying on the role the tree assigns. Rung 2 — relational: the textbox sharing a row with the caption 'Member ID' (occurrence 1). Rung 3 — structural: the textbox at position 0 in reading order, which breaks if a control is inserted before it. Rung 4 — coordinates: last resort, viewport-bound, and the only rung that would still work on a surface with no queryable tree at all.

known_outcomes.name: session_expired
known_outcomes.message: The application signed us out mid-flow. Re-authenticating requires credentials the automation is never permitted to handle, so this cannot be recovered in-loop and escalates to a person.

known_outcomes.name: balance_returned
known_outcomes.message: Member detail panel rendered; the savings balance was read.

known_outcomes.name: member_not_found
known_outcomes.message: No member exists with that ID. A legitimate answer, not a failure.

known_outcomes.name: permission_denied
known_outcomes.message: The member exists but the operating account may not view it.

known_outcomes.name: member_id_not_submitted
known_outcomes.message: The app reports an empty Member ID, so our type step did not land. Our bug.

known_outcomes.name: branch_code_not_submitted
known_outcomes.message: The app reports an empty Branch Code, so rung-2 resolution typed into the wrong field.

dismiss_target.robustness_note: A real button with a stable name; an interstitial this simple needs no fallback rung.
